jobs.title: Director, Finance Data Strategy & Stewardship
jobs.description:
Description

The Experience:

As a member of the Controllership organisation, the Director of Finance Data Strategy & Stewardship will lead the end-to-end strategy, governance, and lifecycle management of Finance data across the enterprise. This role oversees the intake of new data into the Finance data lake, defines data models and governance standards, and ensures the reliability, quality, and compliance of Finance data used for reporting and analytics. The Director will also manage and develop a dedicated Data Governance and Reporting Controls team located in India, responsible for data stewardship, SOX-related data certification, and support for Finance reporting.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Data Strategy & Intake Management
Define and drive the Finance data strategy, aligned with business priorities and downstream reporting needs.
Oversee the onboarding of new data sources into the Finance data lake, ensuring scalability, traceability, and alignment with enterprise architecture.
Partner with Finance, IT, and product teams to assess new data requirements and convert them into actionable data delivery roadmaps.
Data Modeling & Architecture
Lead the design of enterprise-grade Finance data models and semantic layers to support analytics, regulatory reporting, and operational Finance needs.
Ensure metadata standards, master data alignment, and consistent data definitions across systems.
Collaborate with data architects and engineering teams to ensure robust and efficient data pipelines.
Data Governance & Controls
Establish and enforce data governance standards, policies, and stewardship processes for Finance data.
Oversee the definition and monitoring of data quality rules, issue management, and remediation workflows.
Ensure compliance with SOX controls and certification requirements related to financial data and reporting.
Leadership of the India Data Governance Team
Lead and develop a team in India responsible for data governance, data quality operations, and stewardship activities.
Oversee processes related to Finance reporting controls, SOX testing support, and data certification.
Foster a culture of accountability, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.
Cross-Functional & Executive Partnership
Work closely with Finance, Accounting, FP&A, IT, Audit, and Data Engineering leaders to align on priorities and data needs.
Serve as a strategic advisor to senior executives on Finance data risks, data quality, and opportunities to improve reporting and insights.
Drive alignment between business requirements and technical implementation across the data value chain.
Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement
Establish KPIs, dashboards, and operating mechanisms to measure data quality, controls effectiveness, and team performance.
Identify and implement process improvements, automation opportunities, and best practices in data governance and data delivery.
Stay current with emerging technologies and regulatory trends shaping Finance data management.

You're Our Person If...

12–15+ years of experience in data management, data governance, Finance data strategy, or related fields.
Strong understanding of Finance processes, accounting flows, and financial reporting requirements; experience in audit or accounting is a plus.
Proven experience designing data models, managing data lakes, and overseeing data ingestion and transformation.
Leadership experience managing global or offshore teams, ideally in shared-services or GCC environments.
Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence executives and cross-functional partners.

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
About Cressey

Located in Vancouver, Cressey Development Group is a leading real estate firm established over 55 years ago. We create exceptional homes, communities, and commercial spaces that redefine how people live, work, and connect. With a commitment to superior design and quality construction, Cressey continues to build on a legacy of excellence. This is Where Great Places Begin. This is Cressey.

Role Overview

The IT Director reports directly to the Chief Financial Officer and own Cressey's technology stack end to end, from the ERP platform and other business applications to infrastructure, security, and day-to-day support. You will set the department's direction while staying hands-on: configuring and improving systems, resolving integration challenges, and working closely with leaders across development, construction, property management, and other business operations to deliver practical, scalable solutions. You will lead a lean team of five IT professionals, and manage additional support from external partners.

You will thrive in this role if you enjoy running an IT function while staying close to the technology, bring deep application expertise, and are energized by improving systems and troubleshooting problems.

Key Responsibilities

Application Strategy and Delivery
– own the strategy, roadmap, configuration, and ongoing improvement of Cressey’s ERP system (Yardi) and the broader application portfolio, including operational, financial, and reporting systems.
IT Operations and Security
– oversee IT infrastructure, end-user support, cybersecurity, and business continuity, delivered through the internal team and a managed-service partner; own security and risk mitigation, including controls, access, backups, and recovery.
Business Partnership
– partner directly with development, construction, property management, sales and marketing, and finance to understand operational challenges, deliver practical solutions, and support adoption of tools and technology through training and change management.
End-to-End Project Leadership
– lead application initiatives from requirements gathering through solution selection, configuration, integration, data migration, testing, deployment, and optimization, while remaining close to the work.
Integration Ownership
– take ownership of the integration layer between systems, ensuring data flows are reliable, documented, and secure, and removing reliance on any single individual or vendor.
Portfolio and Budget Management –
manage the technology portfolio, including project prioritization, operating and capital budgets, licensing, and contracts, with a focus on cost effectiveness and risk management as Cressey's Yardi footprint grows.
Team Leadership
– coach and develop a lean, service-oriented IT team by setting clear priorities, providing hands-on guidance, and building capability across applications and infrastructure.
Vendor and Partner Management
– actively manage relationships with Cressey's infrastructure and application service partners, ensuring accountability for performance, value, and long-term effectiveness.
Standards and Governance
– establish and refine practical standards for application configuration, data quality, access management, and documentation; this includes appropriate privacy and records management.

Experience Required

Cressey is looking beyond titles and tenure. What matters most is experience successfully running, improving, and supporting an ERP in an environment similar in size, stage, and scale, so you can immediately add value and strategic impact to the IT function.
Applications
- you are proficient in implementing, configuring, troubleshooting, and maintaining various software applications (e.g. Yardi, Sage, MRI, RealPage or similar).
Right-Sized Environment
-you have recently worked in and prefer a lean IT function — a small team supported by external partners.
Vendor Management
- you have managed service providers and implementation partners from both an operational and commercial perspective, including scope, performance, cost, renewals, and overall value.
Communication
- you have built trust with non-technical leaders, translated business needs into practical solutions, and led change management that made new processes stick.
Infrastructure and Security Oversight
- you bring sound judgment and technical knowledge to assess risk and set direction.
Leadership
- you have a demonstrated ability to guide, mentor, and develop team members, while fostering a collaborative and high-performance work environment.
Education
- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology (IT), or related field appreciated, but experience is the primary consideration.

Compensation and Search Process

This role is based in Vancouver and performed primarily in the office with some flexibility for remote work on occasion. Hours can be flexibly scheduled to meet personal and professional needs, while supporting core business hours of 9:30 am - 4:00 pm. Availability for some travel to sites and technical support outside regular business hours, but this is not expected to be significant. Applicants must be willing to undergo a criminal record check.

Interested?

Visit Jane Hill Consulting to apply.

Applicants will be considered through November 6th, 2026 and may be contacted before the deadline. All qualified candidates legally eligible to work in Canada are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority. We thank you for your interest. Qualified candidates will be contacted.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Chief Technology Officer

Position Summary

ICS is an established B2B retail software provider at a pivotal moment. The company is investing strategically in technology to fuel growth, improve customer experience, and optimize operations — and that investment requires modernizing a mature, business-critical platform. We are looking for a transformational Chief Technology Officer to own that mandate.

Reporting directly to the President, the CTO will own the engineering vision and strategy, shape the target architecture and modernization path, and lead the continued cultural transformation to AI-driven development (AI-DLC) across the organization. This is a hands-on, player-coach executive role: the CTO sets direction and leads through managers and team leads while remaining close enough to architecture, cloud, security, product, and delivery decisions to challenge assumptions and intervene when required. The primary mandate is to modernize the legacy platform and the engineering organization around it, while protecting business continuity, customer confidence, and future scalability.

The ideal candidate is a balanced transformation leader who combines executive judgment, product orientation, technical credibility, and disciplined execution — someone who raises standards and makes difficult trade-offs while building trust, developing leaders, and guiding the organization through change with clarity, even under uncertainty.

Key Responsibilities

Own technology strategy, software engineering, architecture, infrastructure, DevOps, and delivery across the organization.
Set product direction and roadmap prioritization, aligning technology investment with commercial priorities.
Lead platform and eCommerce modernization, including migration off the legacy platform, by evaluating rewrite, re-platform, refactor, and phased-modernization options and recommending a target architecture and delivery path.
Establish CI/CD pipelines, observability, and automation to support reliable, predictable weekly releases, and set the cloud and hosting modernization roadmap, including sequencing, migration controls, and rollback readiness.
Embed AI tooling into the development process (AI-DLC) — automated testing, smarter code review, faster iteration cycles — and make AI-assisted development standard practice across engineering.
Own cybersecurity, IT general controls, compliance, business continuity, disaster recovery, and technology risk governance for a platform serving both trade customers and end consumers.
Reduce tribal knowledge by getting institutional knowledge out of people’s heads and into documentation and runbooks, making the platform easier to maintain, improve, and ramp new engineers into.
Lead, develop, and retain a distributed 14-person engineering organization spanning internal, offshore, and external partner resources, setting clear expectations and building a team that ships consistently and owns its work.
Evaluate and prioritize commercially viable customer-facing AI capabilities on their commercial merit, separate from internal AI-DLC tooling adoption.
Maintain selective involvement in strategic customers, major escalations, product advisory discussions, and technically complex opportunities.
Provide periodic Board and executive exposure on modernization, technology investment, strategy, cybersecurity, and risk.

AI and Operating Expectations

ICS is actively investing in AI across operations, product development, and go-to-market execution. The CTO is expected to make AI-driven development the organization’s standard operating model, not an experiment.

Make AI-assisted development a standard practice across the engineering organization, embedding AI tooling into automated testing, code review, and iteration cycles.
Establish the organization’s AI-DLC maturity baseline and a validated target and timeline, and lead the mindset shift required to get there.
Separately assess and prioritize customer-facing AI opportunities on commercial merit, distinct from internal AI-DLC tooling adoption.
Model disciplined AI-enabled decision-making for the engineering organization, verifying outputs and exercising sound judgment with technical and customer data.
Champion new workflows and process improvements that support ICS’s broader AI-enabled operating model and raise team effectiveness.

Required Qualifications

Prior Chief Technology Officer, VP of Engineering, or equivalent executive accountability for a software organization.
15+ years of progressive technology experience, including 10+ years leading software development teams.
Hands-on experience modernizing legacy systems, not theoretical — including demonstrated leadership of a POS or eCommerce platform modernization and/or a migration off legacy platforms.
Track record building or deploying CI/CD pipelines, observability systems, and automation in resource-constrained environments that demanded ruthless prioritization and speed.
Experience leading distributed teams across internal, offshore, and external partner resources.
Executive oversight of cybersecurity, technology risk, operational resilience, and business continuity.
Technical depth paired with business fluency: able to connect engineering decisions to business outcomes and hold credible conversations with the President about what the work means for the business.

Preferred Qualifications

Retail technology, point-of-sale, eCommerce, or payments experience.
Beverage-alcohol, grocery, or specialty retail industry experience.
Cloud modernization leadership on AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud transformation experience.
Adjacent experience in vertical SaaS, fintech, ERP, or other high-availability transaction environments.

What Success Looks Like

Completes a technology, product, and delivery assessment within the first 60 days, establishing baselines and aligning leadership on modernization priorities and decision criteria.
Delivers an agreed target architecture and a funded modernization roadmap by 120 days, with CI/CD and observability infrastructure deployed and the team shipping on a predictable weekly cadence.
Makes AI-assisted development standard practice, with tooling integrated and adopted by the engineering team within the first 120 days.
Reduces tribal knowledge through platform documentation, runbooks, and cross-training, while keeping the technical roadmap locked, communicated, and on track.
Shows measurable modernization progress, stronger delivery predictability, improved product execution, and increased resilience within 12 months.
Builds trust and credibility with the President, the executive team, and the Board through clear communication, sound judgment, and disciplined execution, even under uncertainty.

Compensation And Benefits

Base salary plus revenue sharing.
Long-term incentive: 20% stock option match, subject to the applicable plan terms and vesting schedule.
Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision coverage; retirement program; 4 weeks PTO; flexible work arrangements; fully remote work across the United States and Canada.
Professional development: Annual corporate leadership training (global).

About Innovative Computer Solutions

For over 40 years, Innovative Computer Solutions has served the retail beverage alcohol industry as a trusted, proven, and scalable technology partner. Our solutions are built specifically for wine and liquor retailers and include point of sale, inventory, purchasing, ecommerce, reporting, and integrated payments. ICS is an operating unit of Jonas Software.

Business Unit:

Innovative Computer Solutions Inc

Scheduled Weekly Hours:

40

Number of Openings Available:

1

Worker Type:

Regular

More About Jonas Software:

Jonas Software is a leading provider of enterprise management software solutions, serving a wide range of vertical markets including hospitality, healthcare, construction, education, personal care, fitness, leisure, moving and legal services, to name a few. Within these markets, Jonas is comprised of over 65 distinct brands, each a respected leader in its domain.

Jonas’ vision is to be the branded global leader across these verticals and to be recognized by customers and industry stakeholders as the trusted provider of “Software for Life.” We are committed to technology, product innovation, quality, and exceptional customer service.

Jonas Software supports over 60,000 customers in more than 30 countries. We employ over 6,000 skilled professionals, including industry experts and technology specialists. Across our broader network, we support a global workforce of more than 30,000 employees.

Headquartered in Canada, Jonas Software has a global footprint with offices around the world. We’re a 100% owned subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc., based in Toronto, publicly listed on the TSX (CSU.TO), and a member of the S&P/TSX 60 Index.
